Maintenance Report — MNT-0069-005

Asset: WELL-0069 (SW-24 Well 069, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 08 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 12 Apr 2023 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 93 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0069-0025 on 2023-04-06 Report written: 13 Apr 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0069-0025 showed the wellhead at 22.0 °C with the air at 19.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Rig services2,996
Consumables1,198
Labour (company crew and contractor)12,318
Total24,302

Notes and recommendations

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0069-006

Asset: WELL-0069 (SW-24 Well 069, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 14 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 14 Apr 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 15 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0069-0026 on 2023-04-13 Report written: 15 Apr 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0069-0026 at 11:00 on 2023-04-13 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.6% of the pad area, estimated 2.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 218 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 174 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0069-006 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.86% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0069-024

Asset: WELL-0069 (SW-24 Well 069, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 05 Jul 2025 08:00 · Finished: 29 Jul 2025 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 572 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0069-0138 on 2025-07-03 Report written: 30 Jul 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0069-0138 showed the wellhead at 43.0 °C with the air at 38.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Electric motor (exchange unit)4,919

Maintenance Report — MNT-0069-025

Asset: WELL-0069 (SW-24 Well 069, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 19 Sep 2025 08:00 · Finished: 20 Sep 2025 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 20 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0069-0149 on 2025-09-18 Report written: 22 Sep 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0069-0149 at 10:00 on 2025-09-18 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.0% of the pad area, estimated 0.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 6.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration. This is corrective repair number 4 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 218 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 174 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0069-025 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.42% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0069-032

Asset: WELL-0069 (SW-24 Well 069, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 Apr 2026 08:00 · Finished: 08 Apr 2026 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 116 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0069-0177 on 2026-04-02 Report written: 10 Apr 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0069-0177 showed the wellhead at 17.3 °C with the air at 15.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0069-035

Asset: WELL-0069 (SW-24 Well 069, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 26 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 21 Jul 2026 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 596 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0069-0188 on 2026-06-25 Report written: 22 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0069-0188 showed the wellhead at 36.3 °C with the air at 36.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 23 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
